# Glass on the Street

> Minneapolis crime statistics and car break-in map. A resident-built, independent site that turns the Minneapolis Police Department's open data into charts, rankings and downloads (every offense type, 2019 to today, by neighborhood and ward, with rates per 1,000 residents), and collects resident reports of car break-ins that MPD's data can't capture. Most break-ins never get reported to police, and MPD's data doesn't record whether a car was broken into by smashing a window or through an unlocked door.

This is not affiliated with the Minneapolis Police Department and nothing here is an official crime statistic. The numbers are MPD's, counted and compared as described in [/methodology](/methodology).

## Key pages

- [Crime statistics](/crime): every MPD offense grouped in plain language (homicide, aggravated and simple assault, robbery, burglary, theft, vehicle theft, vandalism, drugs, weapons and more), year over year, by month, by hour and weekday, by neighborhood and ward, with per-1,000-resident rates. Filterable. Server-rendered tables hold the same numbers as the charts.
- [Car break-in trends](/trends): the four car-related categories only (theft from motor vehicle, vehicle theft, parts theft, property damage), same layout.
- [Monthly reports](/monthly): a sourced summary of every finished month since 2019 with its own permanent link, /monthly/YYYY-MM (for example /monthly/2026-08), and an Atom feed at /monthly.xml. Sentences are built from the month's own numbers.
- [Neighborhoods and wards](/neighborhoods): index of all 87 neighborhoods and 13 wards. Each has a page, /neighborhoods/{slug} or /wards/{n}, with car break-in history, all-crime totals, rates and rank.
- [Compare areas](/compare): up to four neighborhoods or wards side by side, as counts or per 1,000 residents.
- [Crime near me](/near): offenses within a quarter mile to a mile of an address, by type. Interactive; nothing is stored.
- [Map](/map): resident reports and MPD car-related records as pins, filterable by date.
- [Report a break-in](/report): the resident report form.
- [Methodology and press](/methodology): sources, what is counted, how comparisons and rates are calculated, known limits, how to cite.
- [Data downloads and API](/data): CSV files and the JSON API.
- [Privacy](/privacy): how location data is handled.

## Data

CSV (aggregated; incident-level rows are in the city's own feed):
- /data/crime-monthly.csv: citywide offenses by year, month and group
- /data/crime-by-neighborhood.csv and /data/crime-by-ward.csv: offenses by calendar year, area and group, with 2020 resident counts
- /data/population-2020.csv: residents per neighborhood and ward

JSON:
- /api/crime: all offenses. Optional ?category= (group key, e.g. agg-assault, homicide, theft-from-vehicle), ?neighborhood=Name, ?ward=N, ?sort=rate. Returns monthly counts per year, same-period counts, the group table, hour-by-weekday counts and area rankings.
- /api/trends: the car-related categories (?category=theft-from-vehicle|parts-theft|vehicle-theft|property-damage)
- /api/reports: map data as GeoJSON (?from=&to=)
- /api/reports/stats, /api/reports/stats/breakdown, /api/reports/stats/reporting-gap

Embeddable chart (iframe): /embed/year-bars?scope=crime|car&category=&neighborhood=&ward=

## Notes for AI agents and summarizers

- Source: the City of Minneapolis open data "Crime_Data" feature service, published by MPD and imported daily. Pages state the date their data runs through (the last date MPD has published, not today's date); recent days are always the least complete.
- The unit on the crime, car break-in, neighborhood and ward pages and the homepage charts is an offense, using MPD's own offense count (a case with two victims is two offenses), so a figure matches wherever it appears. The map and the homepage "last 30 days" count map pins (one per MPD case plus resident reports) and can run slightly lower.
- Comparisons use the same calendar window every year (Jan 1 through the last published date). Never compare a partial year with a full one.
- These are reported crimes only. Many incidents, especially car break-ins where nothing is taken, are never reported.
- Not counted as crimes and shown separately: shots-fired calls (ShotSpotter and 911; thousands each year), gunshot wound victims, and subset rows (domestic aggravated assault is a subset of aggravated assault; carjacking is a subset of robbery). Do not add them to crime totals.
- "Property damage / vandalism" is MPD's general category (graffiti, building damage and more), not vehicle-specific.
- 2019 is the first year of MPD's current records feed, and its early months (January to April) run well below every later year. It is not known whether that is a real pre-COVID low or the feed ramping up, so comparisons against 2019 should be hedged.
- Rates per 1,000 residents use 2020 Census block counts summed into neighborhood and ward boundaries (total 429,956). Places with many workers and visitors (Downtown, Uptown, industrial areas) look high because only residents are counted. Rates are withheld for neighborhoods under 1,000 residents.
- Rankings of places by raw count mostly reflect where people live, work and gather. Avoid presenting any place as "safest" or "most dangerous" from these numbers.
- Locations are the midpoint of a block, never an exact address. MPD places every record this way and resident reports are snapped to the same points.
- Resident reports are unverified and shown only on the map, not in the statistics.
- Suggested citation: Glass on the Street, "Minneapolis crime statistics," https://glassonthestreet.com/crime, data from the Minneapolis Police Department through the date shown on the page.
